page.title: Small observations, held together.
page.intro: A working collection of shore notes, material studies and listening records. Follow a subject, inspect the source, and keep a reading list for your next visit to the water.
page.footer: Fictional demonstration collection. The records, dates and creators are illustrative; they do not report environmental measurements. Reading lists stay on this device.

image.credit: Original vector study / illustrative objects, not field evidence

items.title: A notebook for the turning tide
items.summary: A blank recording sheet that keeps time, weather notes and a small drawing on the same spread.
items.creator: Estuary workshop
detail: The sheet proposes places for observations, not a method for measuring water level. No measurements have been supplied.
Use the separate source field to retain the origin of a real record when adapting this collection.

items.title: Where the salt line dries
items.summary: A sequence of material descriptions from a harbour wall, arranged as reading notes rather than sampled data.
items.creator: Mira Lane
detail: The descriptions are a fictional editorial example. Surface colour does not establish salinity or material condition.

items.title: Listening under the footbridge
items.summary: An outline for noting changes in a soundscape without recording or identifying passing voices.
items.creator: Near Shore Studio
detail: The record describes a possible listening exercise. It contains no audio recordings or claims about a particular site.

items.title: Fragments that travel
items.summary: A reading list about found materials, with room to distinguish a direct observation from a later interpretation.
items.creator: Estuary workshop
detail: No specimen was collected for this demonstration. Replace this record with supplied, traceable source material for a real catalogue.

items.title: Return to the same small place
items.summary: A repeat-visit prompt: keep the viewpoint stable, describe what changes, and leave uncertainty visible.
items.creator: Mira Lane
detail: This is an editorial prompt, not a controlled experimental protocol. The collection deliberately supplies no invented results.
